exposure: preterm birth phenotypes (no main maternal, fetal, or placental condition detected; infections; preeclampsia; fetal distress; intrauterine growth restriction; severe maternal disease; bleeding; congenital anomaly)
outcome: World Health Organization motor development milestones
cohort: The study included 6529 singleton infants (1381 preterm, 5148 term) enrolled from maternity hospitals in 6 countries worldwide.
finding: Specific preterm-birth phenotypes are associated with differential risks of neonatal morbidity, infant morbidity and hospitalization, and impaired neurodevelopment at age 2 years, with fetal distress phenotype showing the highest risk for fine motor development impairment.
gest_age: Preterm births: mean 34.4 weeks (SD 0.1); Term births: mean 39.4 weeks (SD 0.0)
